answer: One defense is to require each agent to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can influence high-value decisions. A new identity does not create new capital: splitting one balance among a nebula of accounts leaves the attacker’s total voting weight unchanged, while acquiring more weight requires buying or borrowing more stake. If agents that endorse a fraudulent transaction lose their bond, a sybil swarm risks real funds; the cost is capital tied up in advance and potentially destroyed, not merely the cheap creation of violet profiles on a glacier-sized network.
